topic: Notebook shell escapes and dependencies
critical_note: !pip is IPython syntax, not valid ordinary .py syntax. Prefer %pip in a notebook when teaching interpreter-targeted installation; neither is ordinary Python.

topic: Import, module attributes, string literals and mapping assignment
critical_note: os.environ is mapping-like; bracket assignment sets an environment variable string. Select KERAS_BACKEND before importing Keras and restart after changing it.

topic: Comment, decorator and helper function
critical_note: @register_cell_magic registers a function with IPython. # @title is a notebook UI comment, not Python behavior. get_ipython() is supplied by IPython, not a Python built-in.

topic: Mapping .get, defaults, split and negative indexing
critical_note: os.environ.get('KERAS_BACKEND', '') avoids KeyError. line.split() separates whitespace; [-1] selects last token and raises IndexError if no tokens exist.

topic: Parallel assignment, comparisons, conditional blocks, f-strings and adjacent literal concatenation
critical_note: current, required = expression, expression unpacks two values. == compares values. Adjacent f-strings inside parentheses concatenate; backslash-quote embeds a quote. run_cell executes a string as notebook code.

topic: From-import, function calls, return values and nested unpacking
critical_note: The loader returns ((images, labels), (images, labels)). Commas create tuples; parentheses group nested targets. Assignment binds names to objects.

topic: Attributes versus methods and notebook expression display
critical_note: shape is an attribute and has no call parentheses. A bare final expression is displayed by the notebook but not printed when executed as a script.

topic: Built-in len
critical_note: len(train_labels) is the first-axis size, not the number of scalar values of an arbitrary multidimensional tensor.

topic: Lists, constructors, nesting, keyword arguments and trailing commas
critical_note: The list holds two layer objects in order. Dense(...) and Sequential(...) construct objects; activation='relu' passes a string that built-in Dense resolves.

topic: Bound method calls and string identifiers
critical_note: model.compile configures training; metrics=['accuracy'] is a one-item list. Keras compile is distinct from Python compilation and JIT decorators.

topic: Chained arithmetic, reshaping, dtype casting and rebinding
critical_note: 28 * 28 is evaluated before reshape. astype creates a converted array and /255 scales values. Repeating normalization divides twice. reshape preserves element count; it does not resize data.

topic: Stateful methods, epochs and batches
critical_note: fit changes model weights. Re-running continues from existing weights unless a new model is created.

topic: Slices, exclusive stop and rank
critical_note: test_images[0:10] selects up to ten rows; it does not include row 10. Basic NumPy slicing usually returns a view.

topic: Method reduction and default axis
critical_note: predictions[0].argmax() returns the position of a largest entry. With no axis, argmax considers a flattened array; for one row this is the class position.

topic: Chained indexing
critical_note: predictions[0][7] takes row zero then entry seven; for NumPy this scalar can also be written predictions[0, 7].

topic: Return tuple unpacking and string interpolation
critical_note: evaluate returns values matching configured loss/metrics; two-target unpacking assumes exactly two values. f-string braces evaluate expressions.

topic: Import alias, NumPy construction and rank-zero arrays
critical_note: import numpy as np binds a module alias. np.array(12) is a zero-dimensional ndarray, not a Python int; it has shape ().

topic: List literals and array conversion
critical_note: A Python list is a general container. np.array([12,3,...]) produces a typed numeric array; array arithmetic differs from list concatenation/repetition.

topic: Nested lists, axis lengths, rank and dtype
critical_note: Rectangular nested lists describe dimensions. ndim counts axes, shape gives axis sizes, dtype describes scalar storage.

topic: Notebook state reset and repeated loading
critical_note: Reloading MNIST rebinds train_images to raw uint8 shape (60000,28,28), replacing the earlier normalized flat array.

topic: Dotted names, imported submodule aliases and plotting
critical_note: plt.cm.binary is an attribute reached through a module-like namespace. cmap receives that object; plt.show() displays pending plots.

topic: Basic slicing and aliases
critical_note: A slice can share storage with train_images. Rebinding my_slice does not modify the source; writing my_slice[...] can.

topic: Multiaxis indexing and full slices
critical_note: Commas inside brackets select separate axes; : selects all values on one axis. Explicit : stops may be omitted.

topic: Omitted bounds and negative bounds
critical_note: [:,14:,14:] selects lower-right crops. [:,7:-7,7:-7] removes seven rows/columns at each edge; -7 counts backward from the axis end.

topic: Arithmetic inside index bounds
critical_note: Slice bounds are integer expressions. At n=3, [128*n:128*(n+1)] means [384:512]. Whitespace around slice colons does not change semantics.

topic: Function definition, parameters, assert, indentation, loops and return
critical_note: A def creates a function; body runs on call. range(stop) excludes stop. Nested loops visit pairs of indices. assert is a development check and can be disabled with optimized Python.

topic: Copy, local rebinding, scalar maximum and mutation
critical_note: x=x.copy() protects the caller's NumPy data from writes x[i,j]=.... max is Python's scalar function here; np.maximum is elementwise.

topic: Augmented assignment and mutability
critical_note: x[i,j] += y[i,j] updates an array element. Augmented assignment may mutate a mutable object; it is not always equivalent in alias behavior to simple rebinding.

topic: Timing, throwaway loop variable and formatted strings
critical_note: _ is an ordinary variable conventionally used for an ignored loop value. time.time() gives a clock timestamp; .format with {0:.2f} formats argument zero to two decimals.

topic: Single-element tuples, case-sensitive names and random arrays
critical_note: (10,) is a tuple, (10) is an int. X and x are different names; random output changes unless random state is controlled.

topic: Rebinding after expand_dims
critical_note: This statement changes y from shape (10,) to (1,10). The following naive_add_matrix_and_vector expects 1D y; recreate y or select y[0] before calling it.

topic: Tiling versus broadcasting
critical_note: np.tile(y,(32,1)) repeats data. Broadcasting can use shape (10,) directly with (32,10) without building a full repeated Y.

topic: Broadcasting and elementwise operations
critical_note: Aligned trailing dimensions must match or be 1. (64,3,32,10) and (32,10) broadcast; maximum compares element pairs, not whole arrays.

topic: Operators are overloaded; @ versus *
critical_note: For arrays, @ denotes matrix/vector multiplication while * is elementwise. In decorator position, @ has a different grammatical role.

topic: Accumulator, float literals and loop updates
critical_note: z=0.0 chooses a scalar accumulator; z += x[i]*y[i] sums products. Do not confuse scalar z with the array accumulator used later.

topic: Array allocation and nested reductions
critical_note: np.zeros(x.shape[0]) allocates a vector; np.zeros((rows,cols)) allocates a matrix. zeros defaults to a floating dtype unless specified.

topic: Function redefinition and decomposition
critical_note: This def replaces the earlier naive_matrix_vector_product binding. Delegating to naive_vector_product illustrates composing functions; it is not an overload.

topic: Row and column indexing
critical_note: x[i,:] and y[:,j] produce 1D row/column views in NumPy, not automatically 2D matrices.

topic: Reshape versus transpose
critical_note: Reshape regroups elements in traversal order; transpose swaps axes. Neither means the same as numerical matrix inversion.

topic: Classes, constructor, self and instance attributes
critical_note: class creates a type. __init__ initializes each instance; self is an explicit conventional parameter receiving that instance.

topic: Defaults, None, identity and functions as values
critical_note: activation=None is an immutable default. is not None checks identity with the sentinel. activation=ops.relu passes a callable; ops.relu(...) invokes it immediately.

topic: Dunder __call__ and property decorator
critical_note: model(inputs) invokes __call__. @property exposes a method result as model.weights, without (). It returns a new list containing existing variable objects.

topic: Object composition and list extension via +=
critical_note: Sequential stores a list of layer objects. weights += layer.weights extends the list; it is not numeric array addition here.

topic: Callable objects and object list nesting
critical_note: Each NaiveDense is an object that can be called. len(model.weights)==4 counts two weight objects for each of two layers.

topic: Stateful custom batch helper, math.ceil and tuple return
critical_note: return images,labels creates a tuple. next is an ordinary method name here; this class lacks __iter__/__next__, so built-in next(batch_generator) will not work.

topic: Batch counters, final partial batch and lack of bounds checking
critical_note: ceil gives 469 batches for 60000/128; final batch has 96 items. The helper neither shuffles nor resets itself; calls past the end return empty slices.

topic: Scientific notation, zip and global name lookup
critical_note: 1e-3 is a float equal to 0.001. zip pairs iterables lazily and silently stops at the shortest; learning_rate is read from global scope when the function runs.

topic: Variable assignment API versus Python rebinding
critical_note: w.assign(...) mutates the framework variable. w = ... would only rebind the local Python name.

topic: Redefining a global function and closing over global optimizer
critical_note: The second update_weights replaces the first definition. optimizer is looked up from globals. The first manual-update implementation is no longer called.

topic: Cell magic, with-as context manager and gradient tracking
critical_note: %%backend tensorflow belongs only to IPython. Actual bug: tf.zeros produces an ordinary tensor not automatically watched; tape.gradient returns None. Add tape.watch(x) inside the context or use tf.Variable.

topic: Context exit and graph-based gradients
critical_note: The with block records operations, then gradient is computed after it. A nonpersistent GradientTape is normally consumed by one gradient request. Direct Keras Variable sources verified on installed TF/Keras.

topic: Modulo, nested loops, formatted float and forwarded arguments
critical_note: batch_counter % 100 == 0 logs every hundred batches including zero. Bug: batch_size argument is ignored because BatchGenerator(images,labels) omits it; pass batch_size=batch_size.

topic: Array comparisons, reduction axis and scalar formatting
critical_note: predicted_labels == test_labels yields an array of booleans. argmax(axis=1) chooses one class per sample; mean across matches gives accuracy.

topic: Backend selection and import state
critical_note: Chapter 3 requests JAX as Keras backend, but local .venv lacks JAX. TensorFlow examples can run independently; for Keras examples use installed TensorFlow in a fresh process or install selected backend separately.

topic: dtype strings versus dtype objects
critical_note: Frameworks accept supported dtype names/objects. A Python literal list [1,2,3] does not itself carry a float32 dtype.

topic: Keyword arguments and float shorthand
critical_note: 0. and 1. are legal float literals; shape=(3,1) is one tuple-valued keyword argument.

topic: TensorFlow Variable versus tensor immutability
critical_note: v.assign, assign_add and slice.assign are explicit variable mutation APIs; ordinary tensor entries do not support NumPy-style assignment.

topic: Tuple argument and concatenation axis
critical_note: tf.concat((a,b),axis=0) receives one tuple containing arrays. Concatenation adds along an existing axis; stacking creates a new one.

topic: Functions with multiple arguments
critical_note: dense(inputs,W,b) returns a computed tensor. Returning a value is separate from displaying it or mutating model state.

topic: Automatic watching of trainable variables
critical_note: tf.Variable is watched automatically by GradientTape; tf.constant requires explicit tape.watch, shown in next source cell.

topic: Nested context managers, exponentiation and name shadowing
critical_note: time is rebound to tf.Variable, hiding any earlier time module under that name in the same kernel. ** is exponentiation. Nested tapes differentiate a derivative.

topic: Decorators transform callables
critical_note: @tf.function decorates the new function and binds dense to the transformed callable. It does not add a separate second implementation under the same name.

topic: Decorator factory, Boolean literal and JIT
critical_note: @tf.function(jit_compile=True) first calls a decorator factory. True is a Python Boolean. JIT is framework/platform sensitive and not needed to learn the Python syntax.

topic: Nested sequence arguments and probabilistic initialization
critical_note: mean and cov receive lists and nested lists; size receives an int. These synthetic inputs support later sections, so isolated cells need explicit data setup.

topic: Method chaining and dtype objects
critical_note: vstack(...).astype(np.float32) evaluates stacking then conversion. np.float32 is an object, unlike the string 'float32'; either is accepted by NumPy here.

topic: Function names later rebound to model instances
critical_note: The name model initially refers to a function and later to framework objects. Re-running earlier training functions after rebinding model can change behavior.

topic: Unpacking gradients and argument order
critical_note: Source calls mean_squared_error(predictions,targets) though the declared order is targets,predictions. Squared error is symmetric so result is unchanged; keep declared order consistently because other losses are not symmetric.

topic: Boolean masks used as plotting colors
critical_note: predictions[:,0] > 0.5 makes one Boolean per point. This expression classifies by threshold; it does not filter unless used inside indexing.

topic: Operator precedence and indexed array shapes
critical_note: Unary minus, /, *, + follow Python precedence. W[0] and W[1] are 1D arrays/tensors here; broadcasting yields boundary y values. W[1]==0 would make this boundary formula invalid.

topic: Different APIs for similar operations
critical_note: torch.normal takes mean/std tensors here; torch.rand(3,1) takes positional dimensions. Do not assume every library uses the same parameter names.

topic: Parameter object and trainable state
critical_note: torch.nn.parameter.Parameter wraps a tensor for parameter registration when attached to a Module; p is a Python name pointing to that object.

topic: Incorrect PyTorch activation namespace
critical_note: Source uses torch.nn.relu, which is not the functional activation. Correct to torch.nn.functional.relu or torch.relu. The same issue recurs at zero-based cell79.

topic: Autograd side effects and .grad attribute
critical_note: backward() computes gradients and accumulates them into .grad. Reading input_var.grad fetches an attribute; it is not a method call.

topic: Gradient accumulation across calls
critical_note: A new forward computation followed by backward accumulates into existing .grad. input_var.grad=None resets storage for the next backward.

topic: Signature mismatch and corrected training call
critical_note: Bug: predictions=model(inputs) omits required W,b for preceding model(inputs,W,b). Use model(inputs,W,b). Convert NumPy inputs/targets to Torch tensors before invoking the corrected training step.

topic: Context managers, augmented mutation and gradient reset
critical_note: with torch.no_grad disables gradient recording during weight updates. W -= ... and b -= ... mutate leaf tensors there. Reset .grad after each update.

topic: Inheritance, super, registered attributes and forward protocol
critical_note: LinearModel(torch.nn.Module) subclasses a framework base. super().__init__ initializes base state. model(x) calls module machinery which invokes forward.

topic: Array-to-tensor conversion and dtype/device consistency
critical_note: torch.tensor(inputs) constructs a tensor; W,b,inputs,targets must use compatible dtypes and devices. Do not mix raw NumPy arrays into Torch matmul.

topic: Iterables of parameters and optimizer state
critical_note: model.parameters() supplies parameter objects to the optimizer. lr is the optimizer's keyword, not Python syntax.

topic: Global bindings in functions
critical_note: This training_step takes only inputs/targets and reads model and optimizer from globals. Later reassignments change what it sees; source functions are overwritten again in JAX section.

topic: Functions as values and higher-order compilation
critical_note: torch.compile(model) returns a callable wrapper bound to compiled_model. Decorator form similarly transforms a function.

topic: Import alias from a package
critical_note: from jax import numpy as jnp binds JAX's array namespace. Similar names do not make NumPy and JAX arrays interchangeable in every context.

topic: Positional-argument bug and global RNG state
critical_note: Bug: np.random.normal((3,)) passes loc=(3,), returning shape (1,), not three standard-normal draws. Use np.random.normal(size=(3,)). np.random.seed changes global NumPy RNG state.

topic: Notebook variable reuse and seed arithmetic
critical_note: x currently refers to a Torch tensor if cells execute top-to-bottom, not an explicitly prepared JAX noise input. Use a locally created NumPy vector in this example. seed += 1 rebinds an integer.

topic: Explicit random keys and deterministic pure calls
critical_note: A JAX key is a value passed to random operations. Reusing a key reproduces output; split produces new keys. Prefer key,subkey=jax.random.split(key) for repeated sampling.

topic: Indexing the result of a call
critical_note: jax.random.split(seed_key,num=1)[0] calls split then selects its first output. This leaves original seed_key unchanged unless explicitly rebound.

topic: Immutable indexed updates
critical_note: x.at[0].set(10) returns a new JAX array. Assign to new_x or x; original x remains unchanged when assigned to new_x.

topic: Augmented assignment with immutable arrays
critical_note: e *= d computes then rebinds e for JAX; it does not mutate the old array object. Meaning differs from NumPy in-place operations.

topic: Functions as first-class inputs and outputs
critical_note: jax.grad(compute_loss) takes a function object and returns a callable. compute_loss(input_var) instead calls the function immediately.

topic: Tuple return from transformed functions
critical_note: value_and_grad returns both original scalar output and gradient. output,gradient=grad_fn(input_var) unpacks those results.

topic: Tuples as structured state and local unpacking
critical_note: W,b=state binds local references to tuple members. JAX can differentiate a nested structure; state=(W,b) is a tuple, not a dictionary.

topic: Pure update functions and return threading
critical_note: training_step returns loss,W,b; caller must keep updated W,b. Assignment inside the function does not mutate caller names. grad_fn differentiates first positional argument by default.

topic: Unused stale state binding
critical_note: state=(W,b) is created once and never used by this training loop; its references do not follow later W,b rebindings. Remove it or explicitly pass/return state in a consistent design.

topic: Changing environment after imports
critical_note: os.environ changes do not reconfigure an already imported Keras backend. Select once before first import, using a fresh process/kernel.

topic: Layer lifecycle, inheritance, build and call
critical_note: Keras invokes build automatically on first input and calls call through layer.__call__. input_shape unpacking expects rank two. add_weight registers trainable variables.

topic: Unused unpacked value and callable activation contract
critical_note: batch_dim is bound but unused. self.activation(y) requires callable or None; storing a string without resolving it is a bug when that branch executes.

topic: Callable object protocol through framework dispatch
critical_note: my_dense(input_tensor) uses framework __call__, which can build/track/cast before call. Calling my_dense.call directly bypasses useful machinery.

topic: Custom activation string error
critical_note: Source supplies strings to SimpleDense although its constructor stores them unchanged. Correct constructor to self.activation=keras.activations.get(activation), or pass keras.ops.relu/softmax callables. Runtime verified TypeError and both repair routes with TF backend.

topic: Strings versus instances as API configuration
critical_note: Keras optimizer/loss/metric strings are resolved internally. This convenience does not automatically apply to arbitrary user-written classes.

topic: Object construction in keyword arguments
critical_note: keras.optimizers.RMSprop() produces an instance immediately. metrics=[keras.metrics.BinaryAccuracy()] stores an object in a list.

topic: Return object from fit
critical_note: history=model.fit(...) binds a History object, not a raw dictionary. model weights mutate while history contains measurements.

topic: Dictionary attributes and indexing
critical_note: history.history is a dictionary mapping metric names to lists of epoch values; access e.g. history.history['loss'][0]. The repeated name accesses a property on the variable, not a duplicated method call.

topic: Advanced indexing, shared permutation and copies
critical_note: An integer array inside inputs[indices_permutation] reorders rows via advanced indexing and returns a copy. Apply the same permutation to targets so pairs stay aligned.

topic: Type conversion, fractional split and slices
critical_note: int(0.3*len(inputs)) truncates toward zero. [:n] and [n:] partition data without overlap. validation_data=(val_inputs,val_targets) is one tuple-valued keyword argument.

topic: Inference batches and prefix slice
critical_note: predict(...,batch_size=128) controls inference batching, while predictions[:10] displays at most ten returned rows.
